buchanan_locke: The named exception to Barclay’s account of his opponents.
juvenal_locke: The Roman satirist quoted by Locke.
winzerus_locke: The writer Barclay cites for the two cases of forfeiture.
caligula_locke: The emperor paired with Nero in Barclay’s examples.
bilson_locke: The bishop whose treatise is cited in section 239.
bracton_locke: The English legal writer named in section 239.
fortescue_locke: The English legal writer named beside Bracton.
polyphemus_locke: The Cyclops in Locke’s comparison of forced peace in the cave.
hingar_locke: The Danish conqueror named alongside Hubba in §196.
hubba_locke: The Danish leader named alongside Hingar in §196.
spartacus_locke: The historical figure in Locke’s counterfactual conquest of Italy.
algiers_locke: The destination in the navigation comparison of §210.
william_conqueror_locke: William of Normandy in the argument about conquest, distinct from the reigning William named in the preface.
drawcansir_locke: The swaggering stage hero invoked in Locke’s plural, Draw-can-Sirs.
king_james_locke: The king whose use of the word commonwealth Locke invokes in Book II, §133.
civitas_locke: The Latin word quoted for comparison with English commonwealth in Book II, §133.
xerxes_locke: The Persian king whose army serves as Locke’s historical comparison.
acosta_locke: The historian whom Locke quotes on the government of peoples in the Americas.
florida_locke: The region named in the quotation from Acosta.
cheriquanas_locke: The people named in the English quotation from Acosta.
brazil_locke: The country named in the English quotation from Acosta.
palantus_locke: The Spartan leader in Locke’s citation of Justin.
justin_locke: The historian Locke cites for the departure from Sparta.
ceylon_locke: The island in the travel account to which Locke refers in Book II, §92.
tsar_locke: The sovereign title Locke compares with the Grand Signior in Book II, §91.
sultan_locke: The Ottoman sovereign title in Book II, §91.
soldania_locke: The place named in the first-edition wording of Book II, §14.
hooker_locke: Richard Hooker, author of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity.
soto_locke: The explorer named by Locke in §153.
homer_poet_locke: The poet cited on the Greek kings at Troy.
carolina_locke: The colony Locke uses as a comparison for settlement by language.
eutopia_locke: The imagined commonwealth Locke mentions in §147.
china_locke: The country whose people Locke names in his discussion of national histories.
ogygis_locke: The ancestral figure named first in Locke’s list in section 141.
brama_locke: The ancestral name in Locke’s list in section 141.
tamberlain_locke: Timur, named Tamberlain in the supplied English.
jeffreys_locke: The judge named by Locke in his comparison of declaring a death sentence with making a law.
oliver_locke: Oliver Cromwell in Locke’s example of how royal power is acquired.
masanello_locke: The former fisherman named in Locke’s comparison of governments.
quixote_locke: The knight whose squire governs the island in Locke’s literary example.
sancho_locke: Don Quixote’s squire, named Sancho Pancha in the supplied text.
peru_locke: The country named in Locke’s citation of Garcilaso.
inca_locke: The people named in the title of Garcilaso’s history.
garcilaso_locke: The historian whose account Locke quotes in Book I, section 57.
procrustes_locke: The mythical host named in Locke’s comparison in section 60.
ainsworth_locke: Henry Ainsworth, whom Locke cites on the eighth Psalm.
grotius_locke: Hugo Grotius, whose words Filmer quotes.
hunton_locke: Philip Hunton, author on limited and mixed monarchy.
king_william_locke: The reigning king in Locke’s preface.
hobbes_writer: Author named in the prefatory reference key.
milton_writer: Author named in the prefatory reference key.
nero_locke: The Roman emperor in the comparison to a literary exercise.
heyward_locke: Writer cited on the rights of kings.
blackwood_locke: Writer cited on the rights of kings.
barclay_locke: Writer cited by Locke on the rights of kings.

locke_act: A deed performed or the exercise of an authority or capacity. Used in the distinction between in act and in habit, and for collective and legislative acts.
locke_providence: God’s foresight and care in ordering events. Uses the native before-and-care construction in its theological sense.
locke_wampum: Shell beads used in exchange, named Wampompeke in Locke’s comparison of currencies.
locke_democracy: Locke’s form in which the community’s majority retains the whole legislative power.
locke_oligarchy: The form in which legislative power rests with a select few and their heirs or successors.
locke_member: A person belonging to the political community whose collective acts Locke discusses.
locke_majority: The greater number of the members whose consent binds the political body.
locke_tobacco: The cultivated leaf named alongside sugar and grain in Book II, §40.
locke_ambergris: The waxy aromatic substance found at sea which Locke uses as an example of acquisition by labour.
locke_reparation: Making good the loss suffered by the person injured.
locke_restraint: Holding an offender back from doing further injury.
locke_sodomy: The historical category of sexual acts Locke names in his argument from precedent. Distinct from incest and adultery.
locke_arbitrary: Power exercisable at the holder’s choice.
locke_charity: Love of a fellow human expressed in the duty to give necessary relief out of abundance.
locke_depend: To need another’s support for one’s subsistence.
locke_scripture_verse: A numbered subdivision cited in Scripture.
locke_septuagint: The Greek version of Scripture to which Locke compares the Hebrew wording.
locke_genesis: The book of Genesis. Its established native book title is Pô in the sealed Bible.
locke_habit: A power said to inhere in a person before its actual exercise, Filmer’s in habit.
locke_property: What belongs to someone, including the rights in life, liberty and estate which Locke groups under this term.
locke_prerogative: Discretionary executive action for the public good where statute gives no direction or would defeat that good.
locke_castrate: To castrate a person. Distinguishes the act in Filmer’s quotation from the standing of the person.
locke_treatise: A sustained written examination of a proposition.
locke_civil_rule: Government considered as the authority of a political community.
locke_principle: A fundamental proposition on which an argument rests.
locke_purpose: The object for which authority is instituted.
locke_preface: The author’s opening address to readers.
locke_fatherhood: The relation of father to child.
locke_make_law: Pertaining to the making of laws.
locke_apply_law: Pertaining to the carrying out of laws.
locke_external_power: Pertaining to a commonwealth’s external relations.
locke_despotic: Power of a master over a slave as distinguished from paternal or political power.
locke_slavery: The condition of being held in slavery.
locke_hypothesis: An assumption to be tested or refuted.
